source: combine deep underground exploration, tool upgrades, and pet collecting. Players dig through blocks, gather rare ores, and unlock new worlds.Step into a vast underground world where every swing of your pickaxe brings you closer to untold riches and rare treasures. As you smash through layered blocks of stone, coal, and gleaming crystals, you will collect valuable ores in your backpack before racing back to the surface to sell your haul for massive profits. Use your hard-earned cash to upgrade to powerful new pickaxes, unlock deeper biomes with higher-tier minerals, and hatch loyal pets that boost your mining speed and multiplier stats. Whether you are playing solo or teaming up with friends to climb the global leaderboards, the thrill of the deep unknown keeps every expedition fresh and exciting.

answers.ask: Should the underground read as bright and cartoony in the usual simulator style, or as a gritty realistic mine?
answers.answer: Use a bright, cartoony simulator style with colorful layered blocks, glowing crystals, and readable ores.

answers.ask: How many depth tiers should there be, and how far down does the deepest one go?
answers.answer: Start with 4 depth tiers, with the deepest tier at 1,000 blocks down, to keep the first build focused while still supporting progression.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: Should the underground read as bright and cartoony in the usual simulator style, or as a gritty realistic mine? A: Use a bright, cartoony simulator style with colorful layered blocks, glowing crystals, and readable ores.
- [author] scale — Q: How many depth tiers should there be, and how far down does the deepest one go? A: Start with 4 depth tiers, with the deepest tier at 1,000 blocks down, to keep the first build focused while still supporting progression.
- [agent_inferred] world_structure — Q: Are “new worlds” separate maps in the first build or depth biomes in one mine? A: Treat them as four unlockable depth tiers in one underground stack beneath a shared surface hub.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a bright, cartoony mining-simulator world with one shared surface hub above four stacked underground depth tiers, the deepest reaching 1,000 blocks down. At the surface, cluster a sell counter, pickaxe-upgrade bench, and pet-hatching pedestal around the mine entrance. Connect the hub to a clear central shaft serving all four tiers. Build each tier as a broad field of colorful layered breakable blocks, with readable stone, coal, ores, and glowing crystals becoming rarer and more visually valuable with depth. Mark the entrance to each deeper biome with a visible progression barrier and give every tier distinct color accents while preserving the same playful style. Keep the mine shared for solo or cooperative digging and make the vertical relationship between surface, shaft, and four tiers unambiguous.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Simulation.

## Shape and preset
Use `world-underground`, a Zone (Surface and Underground Layers), because one surface economy hub connects to four stacked mining tiers. The preset is Mining & Extraction, with its unrequested vehicle-hauling route omitted.

## Config requirements
Use `social-hub` for the surface sell, upgrade, and hatching cluster. Use `resource-shared` for each communal block field. Use `gate-progression` for the visible barriers between four depth tiers. Use the visible side of `trigger-task` for the three surface service stations. Pickaxe stats, backpack limits, money, pet multipliers, and leaderboards are mechanics rather than additional geometry.

## Layout requirements
Place `trigger-task` as three TriggerZone stations at the surface: one sell counter, one pickaxe-upgrade bench, and one pet-hatching pedestal. Place `collectible-nodes` throughout all four tiers, with common stone and coal higher up and progressively rarer ores and crystals deeper down. Keep all nodes inside the shared dig fields.

## Layout components
The build contains one surface hub, one central vertical mine shaft, four stacked depth-tier zones, three service stations, four shared resource fields, and three progression boundaries between tiers. The deepest tier is 1,000 blocks below the surface. Each layer surrounds the shaft and remains separately capturable.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: make each tier plan and the aligned shaft connections authoritative, then dress the surface and four isometric underground layers.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale band is huge vertically because the mine reaches 1,000 blocks down, while separate layer captures preserve ore-level detail. The theme is bright cartoony mining with colorful blocks and glowing crystals. Use `P2` because stacked tiers overhang one another and `P3` because play crosses from the surface into the underground mine.

options.text: A surface economy hub that clusters the sell counter, pickaxe-upgrade bench, and pet-hatching pedestal around the mine entrance.
Each depth tier is a communal shared dig field: a broad field of colorful layered breakable blocks surrounding the central shaft.
Visible progression barriers marking the entrances between the depth tiers (unlock gates to deeper biomes).
Three surface service stations: a sell counter, a pickaxe-upgrade bench, and a pet-hatching pedestal (trigger-zone stations; visible station geometry only).
Ore and material nodes throughout all four tiers: common stone and coal higher up, with progressively rarer ores and glowing crystals deeper down, all kept inside the shared dig fields.

layout_placement.text: Three trigger-zone service stations: one sell counter, one pickaxe-upgrade bench, and one pet-hatching pedestal, all at the surface hub.
layout_placement.where: At the surface around the mine entrance as three TriggerZone stations.

layout_placement.text: Ore/material nodes distributed through all four tiers, with stone/coal more common in upper tiers and rarer ores/crystals deeper down; keep all nodes inside the shared dig fields.
layout_placement.where: Throughout all four underground tiers, inside the shared communal dig fields.

notes: No explicit layout composition framing (foreground/midground/background) was stated in the blob, so layout.composition is empty.

The blob states to place the 'visible side' of trigger-task for the three surface service stations; this JSON marks trigger-task as visible geometry in options, and also includes trigger-task in layout_placement as requested.
The preset Mining & Extraction normally includes a vehicle-hauling route (path-road-vehicle), but the blob explicitly omits it; it is therefore not included.
The schema requires render.then; the blob only specifies render order as topdown first, then dressing in isometric, so render.then is set to 'isometric'.
